assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Covalent bond
items.clue: A shared pair of electrons between two atoms.

items.label: Carbon nanotube
items.clue: A cylindrical fullerene with a very high length to diameter ratio.

items.label: Buckminsterfullerene
items.clue: The first fullerene to be discovered, C₆₀, which has a spherical shape.

items.label: Nanoscience
items.clue: The study of structures that are 1–100 nm in size, of the order of a few hundred atoms.

questions.stem: Which particles have diameters between 1 x 10⁻⁷ m and 2.5 x 10⁻⁶ m?

options.text: Fine particles, which are known as PM2.5
Coarse particles, often called dust
Nanoparticles, which are 1–100 nm wide
Single atoms and simple molecules

questions.explanation: 1 x 10⁻⁷ m to 2.5 x 10⁻⁶ m is 100 to 2500 nm, the range the specification gives for fine particles.

questions.stem: Which list gives only applications of nanoparticles named in the specification?

options.text: Fertilisers, road salt, cement, alloys, and water pipes
Research laboratories and specialised university work
Medicine, electronics, sun creams, deodorants, catalysts
Cement, steel making, glass, plastics, and bricks

questions.explanation: These are exactly the applications the specification lists for nanoparticles.

questions.stem: A particle in smoke is measured and found to have a diameter of 5 x 10⁻⁶ m. Which class of particle is it?

options.text: A nanoparticle, 1 to 100 nm across
A coarse particle, often called dust
A fine particle, only about 5 nm wide
A single atom, about 0.1 nm wide

questions.explanation: 5 x 10⁻⁶ m lies between 2.5 x 10⁻⁶ m and 1 x 10⁻⁵ m, the coarse particle range, and coarse particles are often referred to as dust.

questions.stem: A sun cream made with nanoparticles of a metal oxide is clear on the skin and blocks more ultraviolet light than the bulk form, but its long-term effects on skin cells have not yet been fully tested. Which is the best evaluation?

options.text: It should be used, since being on sale proves it is safe
It should be used, because it blocks the most ultraviolet light
There is nothing to pick, as both creams act in the same way
Better protection and appearance, but long-term effects untested

questions.stem: A factory can buy a catalyst as 5 kg of pellets or as 50 g of nanoparticles that speed the reaction just as much. The nanoparticle form costs more per gram. Which evaluation uses this information best?

options.text: Much less mass is needed, so a higher price per gram may pay off
Neither wins, as the reactive nanoparticles wear out fast
Nanoparticles are better, since they are used up faster
The pellets are better, because the nanoparticles cost more per gram

questions.explanation: Weighs the hundredfold smaller mass against the higher unit price, exactly as the information invites.

questions.stem: Why do scientists say there are possible risks in using nanoparticles?

options.text: They are on sale already, which proves they are safe
They may enter cells and effects are not known
They are far too small to affect the body's cells
They are used up in reactions, leaving a harmful waste

questions.explanation: Their size lets them reach places larger particles cannot, and the long-term effects have not been fully tested.
